steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Dredge chicken breasts in salad dressing, then coat completely with bread crumbs. Place coated chicken breasts in a lightly greased 9x13 inch baking dish and bake in the preheated oven for about 30 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and juices run clear.

raw_recipe.headline: Angela's Easy Breaded Chicken
raw_recipe.description: In a hurry? Just drench chicken with premixed salad dressing and coat with bread crumbs, and dinner is 30 minutes away.
raw_recipe.name: Angela's Easy Breaded Chicken

review.reviewBody:
Great, easy, yummy recipe, Angela! Thank you.

For those complaining about it not being crispy enough, there are lots of basic tutorials on this site. The basic idea is this: lower temp, more time, less browning, versus higher temp, less time, more browning. This is why we broil quickly and braise slowly, and why there are lots of temperatures on our ovens.

So, in short, if you see this recipe, read the reviews, and decide you want it crispier -- boost the temp to 400 and shorten the cooking time by 5 or ten minutes. Or, boost to 425, do for 20 minutes total, and turn halfway through.

I just hate to see a great recipe get "dinged" because people don't read reviews or know how to make some simple changes to suit their tastes. ;)

Used French Dressing. It was all we had. Pounded two breast to 1/2 inch thick. Used a baking rack over a pan. Flipped at half wa point. Baked at 425 for 18 minutes. Chicken came out with a nice crisp to it. Everyone loved it. Thinking you can probably use a lot of different salad dressings with good results.

Yep, it's that easy. I do put chicken in a zip lock with the dressing, though-- it makes it faster and less messy. I use home made bread crumbs which makes it taste better than store-bought. I don't bother to flip the chicken mid-way through cooking. It doesn't matter I have found. But I do bring the chicken to the top rack in the oven to "broil" the chicken about 5 minutes at the very end to make it crispy and golden. My family loves it-- and we have chicken parm this way about once every other month.
Super good! I changed the heat to 400 and did it for 20 minutes, flipping the chicken after 10. I also used ranch instead of italian dressing and it was so good. Definitely recommend.

I made this nearly as written, I used gluten free bread crumbs instead of regular. I also halved the recipe because I had some monster sized chicken breasts. 1 cup of crumbs was more than enough for the 2 monster sized breasts. I also used olive garden italian dressing, it is what I had open in my fridge. That said, this is a recipe where the products you use will matter when it comes to how it tastes. What I did different was baked at 400 not 350. That is the biggest tweak this recipe needs. The chicken was super easy to make and my family liked it.

This was awesome! I appreciate all the comments and suggestions that added to this already great recipe! I added a few tablespoons of melted butter with italian dressing and marinated the chicken for an hour. I baked it in the oven at 400 degrees for a 1/2 hour, found that the breading was still a little soggy, so I put it in the broiler for less then 5 minutes on each side. It came out crispy, flavorful and moist on the inside. We really enjoyed it! I did add some parmesan cheese, italian seasoning and red pepper flakes to the bread crumbs. One cup of them is enough. I also appreciated the suggestion of cutting large pieces of chicken breast in half. Overall, this recipe was awesome and I will definitely be making this again and again! Thanks, Angela!

Can I give MORE then 5 stars?
WOW! GREAT! OK, I did change a couple of things.
FIRST...I used chicken tenders since it's just me and hubby.
SECOND...I make my own bread and had some leftover herb rolls and made my own bread crumbs. 
BUT even with Angela's list of ingredients I think this is a EASY and NO brainer recipe.
I cooked my tenders at 475 degrees for about 15 minutes...checking on them so they didn't over cook.
My hubby said "PLEASE put this recipe in your book". 
THANK YOU Angela...GREAT recipe!

Now this is the kinda recipe I love!! Fast, Easy and tastes great. I chopped up some garlic and marinated with the Italian Dressing for 15 mins. I would suggest NOT marinating it much longer. The acid cooks the chicken making it dry. Ive tried something like this a while back and it turned out horrible bec I marinated it overnight. I also used half breadcrumbs and half parmesan cheese. I will be making this regularly.

This was absolutely fantastic! I googled breaded chicken recipes and this came up. I looked at reviews to tweak things a tad. I too seasoned my bread crumbs. I used garlic salt, onion powder, parmesan cheese, italian seasoning and some other seasonings with rosemary. I broiled the last five minutes to get it crispy. I marinated about an hour. Used Paul Newmans Oil & Vinegar dressing. I also melted butter in the bread crumbs. It was sooooo tender, juicy and flavorful. My boyfriend went back to eat the rest. Thank you! Will make this again and try with other dressings!

I loved this. It was the easiest thing I have made in a long time, but was so tasty! I made my own "breadcrumb" mixture using crushed ritz crackers and basil, thyme, paprika, salt, and pepper. It turned out amazing. I baked at 400 degrees for 20 minutes, flipping them halfway through, and it wasn't soggy at all.
this time I let the chicken sit in the dressing for overnight then coated it with the bread crumbs and baked. it came out so flavorful
Definitely trying this probably to nite! Give reviews later!!!!! Tried it. Not impressed. All the coating came of. Just another boring piece of chicken. Sorry but you missed the mark on this one.

I made the chicken along with broccoli, rice and cheese, and collard greens for the first time. My boyfriend gave me two thumbs up. I baked at 400 degrees, and it turned out with some browned and crispness. Thank you
I make this recipe all the time. It's so easy and everyone loves it!
easy & delicious, what more can you ask for
This was easy, fast and delicious! I had plain bread crumbs, so I sprinkled garlic and onion powder, black pepper, paprika and parsley on top. Yummy!
Didn't have italian dressing or bread crumbs, so I used honey bunches of oats and honey mustard dressing
Amazing. I out done myself. Thank you Angela. I am going to have to make this for my wife and son...Very tasty.....My first time making this....
